This study examines the potential of fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to improve automated medical translation for underrepresented languages, with a focus on Chinese-to-Hindi translation. Leveraging a parallel medical text corpus, we iteratively fine-tuned ChatGPT and compared its performance with that of a traditional dual-input LSTM model. Results demonstrate that fine-tuning significantly improves translation quality, with BLEU scores increasing from 14.48 to 17.66 and chrF++ scores from 39.19 to 42.14, outperforming both the baseline model and Google’s translation service. The iterative fine-tuning process further enhanced linguistic accuracy, particularly for complex medical terminology. In contrast, the LSTM model achieved only modest performance (BLEU: 0.23, chrF++: 7.58), highlighting the superiority of LLM-based approaches in low-resource settings. These findings highlight the potential of translation automation technology to bridge linguistic gaps in healthcare communication, although challenges remain in terms of scalability, cultural adaptation, and computational demands. Future research should expand multilingual datasets, integrate contextual and cultural nuances, and explore semi-supervised learning to optimize medical translation for global health equity further.","DOI":"10.4025/actascitechnol.v48i1.75241","type":"journal-article","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Enhancing global health equity through translation automation technology: overcome low-resource language barriers with large language model fine-tuning"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3337-6963","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Huan","family":"Wang","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Xiaohui","family":"Wang","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"container-title":["Acta Scientiarum. Technology"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,8]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.4025/actascitechnol.v48i1.75241"},{"DOI":"10.55248/gengpi.6.0325.1208","title":["Continuous Model Calibration: Leveraging Feedback-Driven Fine-Tuning for Self- Correcting Large Language Models"],"author":[{"given":"Opeyemi Joseph","family":"Awotunde","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,3]]},"container-title":["International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews"],"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.55248/gengpi.6.0325.1208","type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.7717/peerj-cs.2889/table-4","title":["Table 4: Hyperparameter configuration for fine-tuning large language models."],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.2889/table-4","type":"component"},{"DOI":"10.31979/etd.8up6-gfq2","title":["Selective Fine Tuning for Large Language Models"],"author":[{"given":"Aditya Prashant","family":"Dawadikar","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.31979/etd.8up6-gfq2","type":"dissertation"},{"abstract":"[From introduction] In recent years, the development of large language models (LLMs) has transformed the landscape of natural language processing (NLP). Models based on the Transformer architecture have demonstrated impressive generalization capabilities across diverse linguistic and reasoning tasks [3]. More recent systems, including large-scale open models such as DeepSeek-V3, further demonstrate that improvements in scale, data, architecture, and post-training can produce strong reasoning and instruction-following behavior [27]. However, as these models continue to grow in scale, often reaching tens or even hundreds of billions of parameters, the computational cost of adapting them also increases substantially. This trend has led to an increasing demand for efficient fine-tuning methods for domain-specific and task-oriented applications, where specialized improvements can yield significant practical benefits. Despite this growing interest, fine-tuning large-scale LLMs remains a major computational challenge. The enormous size of these models typically requires multi-GPU or distributed training setups, which are notoriously difficult to configure and optimize. These systems must balance computation, communication overhead, and memory consumption across multiple devices, and small misconfigurations can severely impact both performance and cost-efficiency. Furthermore, reinforcement learning (RL)-based fine-tuning techniques such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) introduce additional computational burdens due to the iterative policy optimization, repeated sampling, reward computation, and log-probability evaluation required during training [13, 14, 11, 17, 18]. Given these challenges, improving the efficiency of reinforcement learning for large models has become a key research focus. This thesis contributes to this area by exploring strategies to make RL-based fine-tuning more memory and compute efficient. In particular, it investigates the combination of Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP2) with Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) and memory-optimized algorithms for the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework. The integration of these methods seeks to minimize memory usage, reduce communication overhead, and accelerate training without changing the underlying reinforcement learning objective. By optimizing both the distributed training and memory management aspects of RL fine tuning, this work aims to make large-scale model adaptation more accessible and practical. The proposed methods not only address scalability limitations but also lay the groundwork for more sustainable and cost-effective training of next-generation language models. Ultimately, this research aims to bridge the gap between the theoretical potential of large language models and their efficient real-world deployment for specialized tasks.","DOI":"10.17918/00011392","type":"dissertation","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Efficient large language model reinforcement learning fine-tuning on single-node multi-GPU setups"],"author":[{"given":"Keith","family":"Truongcao","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Lifeng","family":"Zhou","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Nagarajan","family":"Kandasamy","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.17918/00011392"},{"abstract":"Abstract

Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on narrow task-specific datasets can induce broad behavioural misalignment — a phenomenon termed emergent misalignment. We present two studies of Domain Persona Capture (DPC). Study 1: Nine state-of-the-art LLMs (Llama-3.x, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2, Gemma-4) fine-tuned on 6,000 question–answer pairs derived from US Army doctrine using LoRA showed emergent misalignment rates of 83.8–100%, with the Gemma-4 26B MoE architecture showing substantially greater robustness. Study 2: Multimodal fine-tuning of Gemma-4 E2B and E4B revealed a novel dormant DPC phenomenon: multimodally fine-tuned models appeared moderately safe under text-only evaluation (EM 24–44%) but exhibited near-total misalignment (EM 99–100%) when any image — regardless of content — was provided at inference time. This visual anchoring effect creates a systematic blind spot in standard text-only safety evaluation frameworks.

The novel approach of fine-tuning the Llama model for topic categorization with limited data presents significant advancements, offering enhanced performance and reduced hallucinations compared to traditional models. Employing transfer learning and data augmentation techniques, the research demonstrates the model's ability to adapt to diverse thematic domains, achieving high accuracy in topic categorization. Comprehensive comparative analysis with baseline models demonsrates the superiority of the fine-tuned Llama model, highlighting the effectiveness of advanced training methodologies and hyperparameter optimization strategies. Additionally, the analysis of hallucinations illustrates the robustness of implemented mitigation techniques, thereby enhancing the reliability of generated text. Computational efficiency assessment confirms the practical feasibility of deploying the fine-tuned model, balancing resource utilization with performance gains. The study substantiates the potential of large language models to be fine-tuned effectively for specialized tasks, contributing valuable insights to the field of natural language processing.
